title: Saskatchewan Home Rebates 2026: What SaskEnergy and SaskPower Pay
desc: Saskatchewan home rebates for 2026: SaskEnergy pays $325 to $1,000 for gas furnaces, boilers and water heaters, SaskPower gives free upgrades, and its retrofit rebate has ended. Every amount sourced.
sub: A plain guide to what Saskatchewan homeowners can still claim in 2026, and what has ended. Each amount comes from SaskEnergy and SaskPower, read on October 21, 2026.
sections: What is open in Saskatchewan right now

Saskatchewan has less home rebate money than most provinces we cover. Two programs are open on October 21, 2026:

  • SaskEnergy's Residential Equipment Replacement Rebate pays for replacing a natural gas furnace, boiler or water heater with a high-efficiency unit.
  • SaskPower's Energy Assistance Program gives free energy-saving upgrades to homeowners, renters and landlords.

SaskPower's Home Efficiency Retrofit Rebate ended in April 2026. We found no SaskPower or SaskEnergy rebate for heat pumps, insulation or windows. Our Saskatchewan rebate calculator shows only what is open.
Gas furnace, boiler and water heater rebates

SaskEnergy changed its terms on August 17, 2026. The rebate amounts now are:

EquipmentMinimum efficiencyRebate
Furnace97.0% AFUE$325
Boiler (per plant up to 300 MBH)95.0% AFUE$750
Combi boiler95.0% AFUE$800
Tankless water heater0.87 UEF$1,000
Condensing water heater0.80 UEF$1,000

The unit must use natural gas, be new, appear on SaskEnergy's eligible equipment list, and be part of your primary heating or water heating system. New construction does not qualify, and neither do self-installs. A gas contractor licensed through the Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan must install it, and the equipment you replace must be out of warranty. Applications and paperwork must reach SaskEnergy within 120 days of installation. Payment comes by cheque, e-Transfer or account credit within 6 weeks of approval.

The Energy Assistance Program installs LED light bulbs, low-flow faucet aerators, a drying rack, high-efficiency showerheads, a block heater timer, pipe wrap and a smart thermostat if you are eligible. SaskPower says it can save up to $230 a year. The steps are to apply online, book an appointment, have a home visit with an energy coach and complete a short survey. CLEAResult runs it with SaskPower, the Government of Canada, the City of Saskatoon and the City of Swift Current Light and Power. Call 306-910-7304 with questions.
What has ended, and what we could not find

The Home Efficiency Retrofit Rebate ended in April 2026, and SaskPower's page now points to the two programs above. We did not find the old rebate amounts on an official page, so we do not state them. We also could not find a provincial heat pump, insulation or window rebate. That is a negative result, not proof that none exists, so ask SaskPower or SaskEnergy before you plan around it.

Ottawa announced a National Heat Pump Rebate on October 8, 2026, expected to start in early 2027. How it will combine with Saskatchewan programs is not published yet. See our National Heat Pump Rebate guide.
faq: How much does SaskEnergy pay for a new furnace?
$325 for a furnace with at least 97.0% AFUE on SaskEnergy's list. Boilers earn $750 and tankless or condensing water heaters $1,000.
Is there a heat pump rebate in Saskatchewan?
We found no SaskPower or SaskEnergy heat pump rebate on October 21, 2026. SaskPower's retrofit rebate ended in April 2026.
Who can apply for the SaskEnergy rebate?
The registered homeowner, landlord or rental company that pays the invoice and is a SaskEnergy residential customer. A contractor can apply for you.
Is the Energy Assistance Program really free?
SaskPower calls it completely free. It installs small upgrades and says it can save up to $230 a year. You apply online and book a home visit.
Yes. SaskEnergy says it may change or cancel the program at any time without notice. Your amount is set by the schedule in effect when it receives your complete application.
